content: Laguna Honda Hospital and Rehabilitation Center is a licensed acute-care hospital located in San Francisco, California. The facility offers a comprehensive range of rehabilitation services, including physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech pathology, and audiology. The professional staff includes activity therapists, as well as specialists in medicine, nursing, social work, psychology, and nutrition. The hospital provides skilled nursing services to adult residents of San Francisco who are disabled or chronically ill. This includes specialized care for individuals with conditions such as wounds, head trauma, stroke, spinal cord injuries, orthopedic injuries, AIDS, and dementia. The facility is operated by the City and County of San Francisco and has a capacity of 1,070 beds. A significant expansion project began in the year 2000, with a scheduled completion in 2008. This $400 million initiative aimed to meet updated earthquake safety standards, modernize the hospital's infrastructure, and incorporate advanced technology in both hospital architecture and information systems. The project also added 780 patient beds to the facility. The hospital is located at 375 Laguna Honda Boulevard. Historically, the site has experienced subsurface chemical contamination. In addition to its inpatient services, Laguna Honda Hospital offers outpatient rehabilitation services through the Adult Day Health Center. This program includes the Alzheimer’s Day Care Resource Center, which provides respite care, resource information, and a therapeutic environment for individuals with Alzheimer’s disease. The hospital also operates the Senior Nutrition Program, which serves as a congregate meal site offering nutritious lunches to San Francisco residents aged 60 and older.
